standard_prerequisites.name: Besse volume
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Besse volume of a contact form is the measure induced by (lambda wedge dlambda)^n on the contact manifold.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity bounded in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The branched covering tilde-iota
standard_prerequisites.statement: The restriction of tilde-iota to the interior is an alpha-th fold branched covering map onto the solid cylinder, with the explicit model in the collar coordinates.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows the volume of the model to be compared with the volume form of the normalised contact form.

standard_prerequisites.name: The normalised form tilde-lambda_0
standard_prerequisites.statement: tilde-lambda_0 = dt + pr_1^* nu_0 is the normalised contact form on the interior, with Reeb field d/dt.
standard_prerequisites.use: Its volume form is computed inside the retained proof.

core_obligations: Express the Besse volume of the contact form through the volume form induced by lambda wedge dlambda, and compare it with the corresponding quantity computed from the normalised form (source lines 1235 onwards).
Use the branched covering model to transfer the computation to the collar coordinates, where the normalised form is dt + pr_1^* nu_0 (source lines 1313-1327 are the model used here).
Bound the resulting integral by the volume of the normalised form restricted to the boundary, using the fold number of the covering to control the multiplicities.
Conclude the stated inequality between the Besse volume of lambda and the volume of nu_0 on the boundary (source lines 1265-1268).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the Besse volume through the induced volume form and pass to the collar model.
Bound the transferred integral using the branched covering multiplicities.
Read off the stated inequality against the boundary volume.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:volume_Besse` at source lines 1227-1233: the Besse volume of the contact form is bounded above by the volume of the normalised form measured on the boundary. The author's proof (source lines 1235-1269) runs the computation through the branched covering model of the solid cylinder: the volume form induced by lambda wedge dlambda is transferred to the collar coordinates in which the normalised form is dt + pr_1^* nu_0 (source line 1214-1219 and the covering equation retained as context), and the inequality is then obtained by controlling the multiplicities of the covering and reducing to the boundary volume of nu_0. The statement is a single inequality between two volumes and records neither the transfer to the collar nor the use of the fold number.
